title: Choose Zoro's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Appraisal Sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Appraisal Sheet
options.lineage: A maker's appraisal certificate: full-size ink rubbing of the work, attested fields, one seal
options.thesis: Every project is presented as an attested specimen, not a card: the work at full size, its facts in a ruled table, sealed only when verifiably live.
materials: graphite rubbing on cool white sheet
options.viewport: ZORO set wide and heavy at the top left as a maker's mark, a two-line statement of what he builds beside it, and the first specimen (Lolo Fruits, No. 01) already entering at the fold, its seal visible; contact and resume as plain ruled actions under the statement.
options.risk: Reads stiff if the tables crowd the work; the screenshots must stay dominant and the attestation quiet.

raised.raise: The viridian seal is the only colour on the page and only ever means verified-live: a link that resolves, a message that was delivered.
Nothing is enclosed: projects, capabilities and stack sit on hairline rules and baselines, never inside rounded cards.
Every specimen carries a fixed catalogue number (No. 01, 02...) that holds in the list, the detail page and the URL.

options.label: Release Notes
options.lineage: Changelogs and git history: versioned entries, diffs, tags
options.thesis: Zoro's career as a changelog: each shipped product is a tagged release with what changed and where it runs.
options.viewport: A release header (zoro v2026.10) with the newest shipped project as the top entry, its diff-style highlights and links.
options.risk: Familiar: changelog-styled developer portfolios are common, so it reads competent rather than memorable.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.lineage: Demoscene title screens: bitmap type on an emissive void
options.thesis: The work rides baselines over a black void; depth is rank.
options.viewport: One still ivory line naming Zoro over drifting grey dust.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hiring managers lose clarity, and black plus one amber is the category's dark default.
options.kept: Nothing enclosed by boxes; content rides baselines and rules.

options.label: Sticker Album Spread
options.lineage: Collector albums with numbered slots and ghosted gaps
options.thesis: Projects as numbered slots in a fixed set.
options.viewport: A spread of numbered project slots.
options.case: Fuses poorly: empty slots would advertise missing work on a portfolio.
options.kept: Fixed catalogue numbering for every project.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Fuses poorly: the portfolio has almost no honest metrics to count, and inventing them is forbidden.
options.kept: One colour, used only for a lit (live) state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio everyone ships, executed well: dark ground, gradient hero, bento grid of project cards.
canonCard.viewport: Big name and role headline over a gradient, CTA pair, project card grid below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of others by design; it is also what your brief asks to move away from.
